theoryOfChange: The Muslim Community Network (MCN) has a published impact framework, as evidenced by their 'Our Impact' page, which details their 'measurable impact' across various programs. This page presents statistics and outcomes for their diversity education, civic education, and self-defense training programs, such as '86.6% Increased understanding of Islam after diversity workshops' and '100% Proficiency in NYC Human Rights protections after civic education'. Their 'Community Education' page further elaborates on how their education programs 'deliver measurable change'. Additionally, the 'MCN Hate Crime Prevention Report 2022' serves as a results framework for their hate crime prevention initiative, outlining community safety training, survey data collection, and policy advocacy, along with survey results and policy recommendations. The 'MCN Impact Academy' also outlines a program strategy with workshop tracks designed to strengthen cultural understanding, community safety, and civic participation.

rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 2003, the Muslim Community Network (MCN) uses civic education and leadership training to empower Muslims in New York City [2]. In FY2025, the organization managed <cite id="1">$1,153,075 in total revenue</cite> to support its community initiatives. MCN maintains an <cite id="5">overall rating of 87.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite>. The charity directs <cite id="5">80.1% of its expenses to programs</cite>, meeting industry standard benchmarks. While MCN tracks three outcome metrics and earned a Candid Platinum Seal [2], its CEO compensation of <cite id="1">$120,333 represents over 10% of total revenue</cite>, which presents a governance consideration for smaller nonprofits. MCN remains <cite id="2">zakat-eligible</cite> with dedicated funds supporting vulnerable populations.
